title: Tarn Taran, 1921
hookLine: reformers were attacked seeking to take over the gurdwara

lines: A SACRED POOL SOUTH OF AMRITSAR.
cards: Early in 1921, a band of reformers walks into a town south of Amritsar, where a gurdwara stands beside a wide sacred pool; tradition says Guru Arjan founded the town.
They've come, singing, to ask the priests who hold the shrine to hand it over to the Panth. They talk, and wait to be heard. Night falls.
They're still there, waiting, when the priests' men come at them with weapons.

teach.h: THEY CAME TO TAKE OVER THE SHRINE.
teach.b: The reformers accused the custodians at Tarn Taran of allowing practices that went against the Gurus' teaching, and of treating the shrine's offerings as their own.
They came to take over its management for the newly formed committee.
Accounts say that while they waited, the priests and the men with them attacked, striking the reformers with sticks and blades. Several were badly wounded, and some died of their wounds.
The reformers didn't answer the attack with an attack.
They held their ground and cared for the wounded, and in the end the shrine passed to the Panth's management. Calm, here, didn't mean quiet.

teach.h: FRIGHTEN NO ONE, FEAR NO ONE.
teach.b: It meant not letting someone else's violence choose your next move. In a salok at Ang 1427 of the Guru Granth Sahib, Guru Tegh Bahadur praises the one who frightens no one and fears no one.
Both halves matter: they came without frightening anyone, and didn't run when they were frightened.
Tradition explains the name Tarn Taran as a boat that carries people across. That night, the people at the pool needed something to carry them through, and they found it in staying still.

how: Sikhs visit the gurdwara at Tarn Taran, with its large sarovar, as a historic shrine; the reformers who died there are remembered among the martyrs of the gurdwara reform movement.

games.why: they stayed and waited. while they waited, the priests' men attacked them; they held their ground, and the shrine in the end passed to the Panth's management.

practice: Bring to mind a moment when someone came at you with sharp words, and notice whether your body still reacts: the jaw, the shoulders, the chest.
On each slow breath out, let the jaw go, then the shoulders, not giving in, just refusing to let someone else's anger set your pace. If you pray, say Waheguru on the breath out.

wordCard.voice: Tarn Taran. A gurdwara town south of Amritsar, where reformers who came to talk were attacked at night and held their ground. Today's word.
